None of the three solutions is verifiably correct.

**Solution 1 (answer 0):** The argument has a gap. Two distinct \(t\)-subsets of \(N(v)\) meet in at most one vertex, but a family of \(t\)-subsets of a \(d\)-set with pairwise intersections at most 1 can have size \(\Theta(d^2)\), not \(O(d)\). So the bound \(C(G)=O_t(e(G))\) is not established. A zero limit also seems unlikely: pair-counting suggests \(\Theta(n^2)\) copies of \(K_{t,t}\) may be attainable.

**Solution 2 (answer \(1/t!\)):** The construction is asserted rather than derived. The claim that every pair in one part has exactly \(t\) common neighbours, combined with the count \(n_e^2/t!\), is not justified. Counting t-sets with a common neighbourhood of size \(t\) gives constants that depend on \(t\) in a different way, and I could not confirm \(1/t!\).

**Solution 3 (answer 1):** The reasoning is incoherent and explicitly guesses ("it is highly probable that the limit is 1"). It gives no valid argument.

I could not determine the true value of the limit, so I cannot select any of these as correct.

CHOICE: NONE
